chunks: As for what was narrated by Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abi Khadijah, from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, who said:
He was asked about a mouse that falls into a well. He said: “If it dies and does not become putrid, then forty buckets; and if it swells in it and becomes putrid, all the water is to be drawn out.”
So his statement, “If it does not become putrid, forty buckets are drawn,” is interpreted as recommendation, based on the indication of the reports we presented earlier.

key_terms.أَرْبَعِينَ دَلْوًا: forty buckets to be drawn from the well
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ: the transmitted reports used as evidence
key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well whose water is being discussed
key_terms.الْفَأْرَةِ: a mouse, the dead animal discussed in the ruling
key_terms.نُزِحَ الْمَاءُ كُلُّهُ: all of the well water is to be drawn out

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a mouse falls into a well and dies in it?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling concerning a mouse falling into a well and distinguishes between the case where it dies without putrefying and the case where it swells and becomes putrid. The closing statement clarifies that drawing forty buckets in the first case is understood as recommended rather than obligatory, in light of earlier reports.
